question: Assume today is 2026-03-21. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the total value of New Zealand's goods exports in March 2026 (actual monthly value, not seasonally adjusted), in New Zealand dollars (NZD), as it will be first reported in Stats NZ's monthly Overseas merchandise trade release.

target.what: Total value of New Zealand's goods exports (merchandise exports, valued free on board, actual and not seasonally adjusted) for March 2026, as it will be first reported in Stats NZ's monthly Overseas merchandise trade release.
target.unit: NZD (total goods export value for March 2026, actual, not seasonally adjusted)
target.caveats: Working interpretation is the headline exports series in Stats NZ's Overseas merchandise trade: merchandise goods exports valued FOB in NZD, actual (not seasonally adjusted), including re-exports per Stats NZ definitions; services are excluded. The first-reported March 2026 value is provisional and

candidates.perspective: Stats NZ published monthly export series; analyst anchoring on recent actuals and seasonality.
candidates.hypothesis: The March 2026 headline export value is closely tied to March 2025 and to y/y growth in Jan-Feb 2026; historical March/February ratios and recent monthly revisions can form an anchor. Symbolically: March_2026 ~ March_2025 * (1 + recent_yoy_growth) * seasonal_adjustment, or latest run-rate * March/Feb seasonal factor.
candidates.data_to_find: Stats NZ Overseas merchandise trade actual monthly goods export values in NZD, not seasonally adjusted, for March 2024, March 2025, January 2026, February 2026 and surrounding months; the release calendar and publication date for the February 2026 release; any pre-cutoff revision. Minimum: February 2026 and March 2025 values plus adjacent February/March history.
search_hints: Stats NZ Overseas merchandise trade February 2026 exports
New Zealand goods exports March 2025 NZD actual
Stats NZ export values monthly table 2024 2025 2026

candidates.perspective: commodity-level export values and price indicators.
candidates.hypothesis: Total exports is the sum of major commodity groups; March 2026 value can be built from latest available commodity export values adjusted by March 2026 price and volume signals for dairy, meat, logs/wood, fruit, fuels, machinery, seafood and other groups. Symbolically: Total = sum(commodity_value_recent * price_index_change * volume_index_change) plus uncovered residual.
candidates.data_to_find: Stats NZ latest monthly export values by commodity or HS group for January/February 2026 and March 2025; GlobalDairyTrade auction prices and dairy volumes; ANZ world commodity price index or NZ export price indices; meat, log and fruit prices and shipment data; shares of major commodity groups. Minimum: February 2026 commodity values and March 2026 price direction for top groups.

candidates.perspective: macro forecasters and market economists publishing NZ trade forecasts before cutoff.
candidates.hypothesis: If a Q1 2026 or March 2026 goods-export forecast exists, March can be derived as the Q1 forecast minus published January and February actuals, or taken as the March forecast directly, subject to definitional consistency. Symbolically: March_2026 ~ Q1_forecast - Jan_actual - Feb_actual.

Minimum: one Q1 goods-export forecast plus January/February actuals, or one March forecast.

Symbolically: March_value ~ sum(observed_partial_volume * days_scale * unit_value) for covered commodities plus residual.

candidates.perspective: seasonal and calendar base rates for March within annual and quarterly exports.
candidates.hypothesis: March typically accounts for a stable share of Q1 or annual goods exports; applying that share to a known or forecast Q1/annual total, then adjusting for working days and commodity seasonality, gives an independent route. Symbolically: March_2026 ~ Q1_2026_total * March_Q1_share_adjusted_for_working_days.
candidates.data_to_find: Historical monthly goods export values to compute March share of Q1 and annual exports; Q1 2026 or annual 2026 export forecast or total; working-day and Easter timing for March 2026 versus history; dairy and lamb seasonality. Minimum: March Q1 share from recent years and a Q1 total forecast or annual total.

Symbolically: March_value ~ export_entry_count * average_value_per_entry, adjusted for coverage and timing.

candidates.perspective: disruption and news signals affecting March 2026 export flows and prices.
candidates.hypothesis: March 2026 shocks such as weather or drought, port congestion, China demand or tariffs, biosecurity issues, shipping schedules and exchange-rate moves can shift the historical or commodity-based estimate; measurable exposure should be used to adjust the chosen route. Symbolically: March_value = baseline_estimate * (1 + net_shock_effect).

Minimum: dated event and affected export volume or value share.

assumptions.name: March 2026 to February 2026 total goods export ratio
assumptions.rationale: March is normally a seasonal peak for New Zealand goods exports relative to February, especially for dairy, meat and fruit. p34 (March 2025 record) and p8 (February 2026) are different years, so they only bound the plausible ratio; recent March/February ratios for total goods exports are generally modestly above one. The range is wide because commodity timing and revisions can shift the ratio.
assumptions.applies_when: Used to scale the latest observed monthly export value p8 to March 2026 when the March seasonal premium is similar to recent history.
assumptions.falsified_by: March 2026 release or high-frequency port/customs data showing March exports at or below February, or a large revision to p8.

assumptions.name: March 2026 to March 2025 total goods export change factor
assumptions.rationale: March 2025 was a record-high month (p34). Current evidence is mixed: February 2026 exports were solid (p8), but the annual goods deficit remains (p17), and energy prices have risen (p48-p50). Without January-February 2025 monthly comparators, a near-flat central factor with a wide range is appropriate.
assumptions.applies_when: Used to carry the March 2025 actual to March 2026 when year-on-year growth is near flat.
assumptions.falsified_by: January-February 2025/2026 monthly data showing a clear high or negative y/y growth, or commodity price/volume data implying a large move.

assumptions.name: Average value per customs export entry, March 2026
assumptions.rationale: p59 gives 6,226 export entries in one study week, while p34 gives a record March 2025 export total. Combined with about four weeks per month, these imply average entry values in the low hundreds of thousands of NZD. March mix is high-value dairy/meat, but entry size is volatile, so the range is wide.
assumptions.applies_when: Used with p59 weekly entry count scaled to a month to proxy March 2026 total export value.
assumptions.falsified_by: Customs or Stats NZ data on March 2026 export entry counts and values, or evidence that the p59 study week has atypical entry size.

assumptions.name: March 2026 export-entry count relative to 2025 average week
assumptions.rationale: p59 is a late-August/early-September 2025 study week, not March. March is often seasonally busier for dairy, meat and fruit export entries, so a modest upward adjustment is plausible; the wide range covers study-week and seasonal mismatch.
assumptions.applies_when: Used to adjust the p59 weekly entry count to March 2026 monthly total entries.
assumptions.falsified_by: Monthly Customs entry counts for March 2026 or seasonal entry-count data showing March below the 2025 study week.

kept.name: March 2026/February 2026 seasonal ratio relative to average March/February ratio in 2024 and 2025
kept.rationale: Observed March/February ratios from 2024 and 2025 provide the seasonal anchor; this factor allows a modest 2026 deviation from that average. February 2026 p8 is used as the current level anchor.
kept.applies_when: March 2026 seasonal timing is similar to 2024-25 and there is no large port, biosecurity or working-day disruption.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence of an unusual March dairy/meat/fruit shipping peak, a major port closure, or a large working-day effect distinct from 2024-25.

kept.name: Average value per customs export entry, March 2026
kept.rationale: p59 gives a weekly export-entry count. Scaling to a monthly rate and calibrating against the March 2025 total p34 implies an average value per entry in this range; uncertainty covers commodity prices, high oil/freight costs and entry-size mix.
kept.applies_when: The customs entry count per month is comparable to the TRS study-week rate and average export value per entry is not dominated by a few unusually large aircraft/fuel shipments.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that the TRS week was not representative or that average export value per entry shifted materially because of large single shipments or a changed entry-size distribution.

kept.name: March 2026 export-entry count relative to the 2025 TRS study-week monthly rate
kept.rationale: p59 is a single week in August-September 2025, not a March average. March is often a peak month, but entry counts depend on shipment consolidation, so the central value is neutral and the range is wide.
kept.applies_when: March 2026 export-entry counts per week are within roughly plus or minus 10-12% of the scaled TRS study-week rate.
kept.falsified_by: Observed March 2026 manifest or entry counts far outside the range, or known port congestion/schedule changes shifting clearance timing.

kept.name: March 2026/March 2025 change factor for milk powder, butter and cheese exports
kept.rationale: March 2025 dairy exports were very strong, up 35% per p38, creating a high base. February 2026 total exports were about flat year-on-year versus p65, and no 2026 dairy price/volume data are available here.
kept.applies_when: Global dairy prices and New Zealand dairy export volumes do not move far from their early-2025 relationship.
kept.falsified_by: GDT auction or dairy export volume data showing a large 2026 price or volume swing.

kept.name: March 2026/March 2025 change factor for meat and edible offal exports
kept.rationale: March 2025 meat exports were up 34% per p40, a high base. Recent total export growth is roughly flat, and no March 2026 meat price/volume data are available.
kept.applies_when: Meat prices, slaughter volumes and export demand are broadly similar to March 2025.
kept.falsified_by: Large changes in lamb/beef prices, Chinese demand, or slaughter/processing volumes.

kept.name: March 2026/March 2025 change factor for all other goods exports
kept.rationale: The residual includes fruit, machinery, logs/wood, seafood, fuels and other manufactures. February 2026 total exports were roughly flat year-on-year, but high oil prices and China demand could shift nominal values.
kept.applies_when: The heterogeneous other-goods groups move roughly in line with the recent total export trend.
kept.falsified_by: Large moves in log prices, China demand, seafood volumes, or fuel exports.

The best estimate for New Zealand's total goods exports (merchandise exports, FOB, actual and not seasonally adjusted) for March 2026 is [[estimate]] [[unit]] ([[interval_level]] interval [[p10]] to [[p90]] [[unit]]).

Two routes were combined with equal weight per block. The first scales February 2026 exports of [[p8_value]] by observed March/February ratios from 2025 ([[p34_value]] over [[p65_value]]) and 2024 (recovered from [[p36_value]] and [[p66_value]]), adjusted by assumption a1 ([[a1_value]], range [[a1_low]] to [[a1_high]]). The second scales the customs study-week entry count [[p59_value]] to a monthly rate, times assumed average value per entry a2 ([[a2_value]]) and entry-count factor a3 ([[a3_value]]).

The main risk is that a2 and a3 are analyst assumptions, not observations, and the study week may not represent March 2026. Better evidence would be actual March 2026 customs entry counts and commodity-level export values.

Key assumptions (proposed by the analyst model, not observed; code samples each one between the bounds shown):
- a1 March 2026/February 2026 seasonal ratio relative to average March/February ratio in 2024 and 2025: [[a1_value]] dimensionless, range [[a1_low]] to [[a1_high]] (range widened by code); used by m1. Overturned by: Evidence of an unusual March dairy/meat/fruit shipping peak, a major port closure, or a large working-day effect distinct from 2024-[n].
- a2 Average value per customs export entry, March 2026: [[a2_value]] NZD per entry, range [[a2_low]] to [[a2_high]] (range widened by code); used by m2. Overturned by: Evidence that the TRS week was not representative or that average export value per entry shifted materially because of large single shipments or a changed entry-size distribution.
- a3 March 2026 export-entry count relative to the 2025 TRS study-week monthly rate: [[a3_value]] dimensionless, range [[a3_low]] to [[a3_high]] (range widened by code); used by m2. Overturned by: Observed March 2026 manifest or entry counts far outside the range, or known port congestion/schedule changes shifting clearance timing.

Method details (computed by code):
- m1 formula_mc: p8 * mean(p34 / p65, (p34 - p36) / (p65 - p66)) * a1; Monte Carlo P10 to P90 [[m1_mc_p10]] to [[m1_mc_p90]]; result unit NZD converted to NZD; own 80% width [[m1_width]] (Monte Carlo of the formula inputs)
- m2 formula_mc: p59 * k_weeks_per_year / k_months_per_year * a2 * a3; Monte Carlo P10 to P90 [[m2_mc_p10]] to [[m2_mc_p90]]; result unit (NZD/month) * 1 month converted to NZD; own 80% width [[m2_width]] (Monte Carlo of the formula inputs)
- Combination: [[n_blocks]] block(s), equal weight per block (methods whose inputs overlap by at least half form one block; backtest errors set widths, not weights): B1 = m1: [[block1_value]] (width [[block1_width]], Monte Carlo of the formula inputs); B2 = m2: [[block2_value]] (width [[block2_width]], Monte Carlo of the formula inputs). Estimate = the geometric mean of the two blocks.

The best estimate for New Zealand's total goods exports (merchandise exports, FOB, actual and not seasonally adjusted) for March 2026 is 7,509,893,078 NZD (80% model-based interval 4,533,940,855 to 12,439,177,274 NZD).

Two routes were combined with equal weight per block. The first scales February 2026 exports of 6,630,000,000 NZD by observed March/February ratios from 2025 (7,590,000,000 NZD over 6,700,000,000 NZD) and 2024 (recovered from 1,200,000,000 NZD and 954,000,000 NZD), adjusted by assumption a1 (1, range 0.7065 to 1.413). The second scales the customs study-week entry count 6,226 export entries to a monthly rate, times assumed average value per entry a2 (280,000) and entry-count factor a3 (1).

The main risk is that a2 and a3 are analyst assumptions, not observations, and the study week may not represent March 2026. Better evidence would be actual March 2026 customs entry counts and commodity-level export values.

Key assumptions (proposed by the analyst model, not observed; code samples each one between the bounds shown):
- a1 March 2026/February 2026 seasonal ratio relative to average March/February ratio in 2024 and 2025: 1 dimensionless, range 0.7065 to 1.413 (range widened by code); used by m1. Overturned by: Evidence of an unusual March dairy/meat/fruit shipping peak, a major port closure, or a large working-day effect distinct from 2024-[n].
- a2 Average value per customs export entry, March 2026: 280,000 NZD per entry, range 197,104 to 394,208 (range widened by code); used by m2. Overturned by: Evidence that the TRS week was not representative or that average export value per entry shifted materially because of large single shipments or a changed entry-size distribution.
- a3 March 2026 export-entry count relative to the 2025 TRS study-week monthly rate: 1 dimensionless, range 0.7099 to 1.42 (range widened by code); used by m2. Overturned by: Observed March 2026 manifest or entry counts far outside the range, or known port congestion/schedule changes shifting clearance timing.

Method details (computed by code):
- m1 formula_mc: p8 * mean(p34 / p65, (p34 - p36) / (p65 - p66)) * a1; Monte Carlo P10 to P90 4,586,110,893 to 12,095,869,721; result unit NZD converted to NZD; own 80% width x/÷1.62 (Monte Carlo of the formula inputs)
- m2 formula_mc: p59 * k_weeks_per_year / k_months_per_year * a2 * a3; Monte Carlo P10 to P90 4,495,168,211 to 12,809,753,397; result unit (NZD/month) * 1 month converted to NZD; own 80% width x/÷1.69 (Monte Carlo of the formula inputs)
- Combination: 2 block(s), equal weight per block (methods whose inputs overlap by at least half form one block; backtest errors set widths, not weights): B1 = m1: 7,445,334,285 (width x/÷1.62, Monte Carlo of the formula inputs); B2 = m2: 7,575,011,663 (width x/÷1.69, Monte Carlo of the formula inputs). Estimate = the geometric mean of the two blocks.
- Interval: root mean square of the block widths x/÷1.66; Birge ratio 0.03 (not above one, so no widening); final width x/÷1.66.

residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.

The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
